column2: The 22nd amino acid used to build proteins, found in 2002 in microbes that make methane. Its code is UAG, which in almost every other living thing means "stop".
The amino acid in tea that's said to take the edge off the caffeine. It's on so many "focus" supplement labels that it's less obscure than it sounds.
The amino acid bacteria start every protein with, and so do mitochondria, a clue to their bacterial past. Your immune system treats it as a sign of bacteria and homes in on it.
